relationshipToReleaseCapabilities: ADDITIVE. GET /release/capabilities serves RELEASE_CAPABILITIES_R8_3.4 (asOf 2026-08-26, 25 rows, OBSERVED at HEAD 19920c0f by executing the committed app) with a four-state vocabulary (ENABLED / LIMITED / DISABLED / EXPERIMENTAL_INTERNAL). That registry is the SERVER's statement about itself and is not replaced. This registry is the PRODUCT's statement about what v1 ships, in the five-state vocabulary NEW3 was asked for, and every row names the runtime row it derives from. Where the two disagree, the runtime registry wins on fact and this one wins on shipping decision. R14 CORRECTION: R13 recorded R8_3.3, 24 rows, and 'still serves NO platform dimension - the string platform appears nowhere in its payload'. All three are now false. PER-PLATFORM SERVING EXISTS: the route accepts X-Lawmind-Platform (header, wins) or ?platform= (fallback) and returns a RESOLVED per-platform view {registryVersion, asOf, platform, capabilities, platformOverrides}. A caller that sends neither still gets the three-key release-wide envelope, byte-identical to before. The per-platform truth is therefore enforceable at RUNTIME as well as at review time. Note the shipped shape is NOT the capabilities[].platforms shape R13 A3 specified; A3 is withdrawn and the shipped shape is adopted as canonical in docs/product/RCC_V1_API_CONTRACT_R14_AMENDMENT.md A4.

stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1: Ships in v1, to every user, with the stated coverage and the stated uncertainty rendered.
stateVocabulary.INTERNAL_EXPERIMENTAL: Runs, is measured, is never reachable by a user in v1. No public surface, no marketing claim.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_NOT_READY: The gap is OURS — code, coverage, or an unmeasured property. Closing it is our work.
stateVocabulary.DISABLED_EXTERNAL_BLOCK: The gap is NOT ours — an authorization, a credential, a registrar's answer. No amount of our work closes it.
stateVocabulary.POST_V1: Deliberately out of v1 scope. Not a gap.
stateVocabulary.ENABLED_V1_KILLABLE: Ships in v1 on this platform, AND carries a capability kill switch that can disable it on this platform alone without disabling the capabilities named in `mustNotDisable`. Used where a platform policy risk is real but unproven.

iosKillSwitch.reason: Apple guideline 5.1.1(viii): an app compiling personal information from any source not obtained directly from the user - public databases included - can be rejected. Case-first design is the correct mitigation and is NOT a guarantee.
iosKillSwitch.degradeBehaviour: VISIBLE. When the switch is active, party-name input degrades to case-number / citation / CNR search with a stated message. It never silently vanishes - a silent disappearance produces support load and a feature-parity claim problem.
iosKillSwitch.servedOrBuildTime: SERVED. Corrected in R14 from R13's 'BUILD_TIME today'. The kill switch is runtime, not build-time-only: GET /release/capabilities resolves search.party_name per platform, and a platform override narrows it for that platform alone. Flipping it is a server-side config change, NOT an App Store release - which is the whole reason the switch exists. The override map is EMPTY at HEAD (platformOverrides: [] on every platform), which is the correct unflipped state: roadmap v7.1 section 9.5 says ship the switch, not disable the capability.
iosKillSwitch.narrowOnly: A platform override may take a capability DOWN and never UP - enforced in committed code by a strict narrowness comparison, and covered by committed tests. So the switch can never become a back door that enables something the release-wide registry refuses.
iosKillSwitch.mustNotDisableVerifiedBy: services/api/src/search/party-search-platform.test.ts, run at HEAD 30 Aug: 17 pass, 0 fail. It asserts that no neutral citation, reporter citation, CNR, case number or 'X v. Y' title classifies as party_name, so flipping the switch cannot take exact identity with it.

capabilities.coverageDefinition: MEASURED across six narrowing scopes of one query ('bail'). ADMITTED: one named court + 3 days -> 5 results in 154.6 ms; one named court + 1 month -> 5 results in 418.1 ms. REFUSED: one named court + 8 months; courts:[hc] category + 1 month at 262.6 ms; courts:[hc] + 29 days at 207.4 ms; unfiltered at 2.9 ms. capabilities.whyNotReady: SUPERSEDED IN R14, AND THE MECHANISM WAS RESTATED. R13 said, reading retrieve.ts at the Day-0 seal, that 'filters is a parameter of that same function and is NOT consulted before the refusal', so 'the bound is corpus-wide while the query is not'. READ FROM CURRENT HEAD 19920c0f that is no longer the mechanism. ADMISSION IS POPULATION-SHAPED, in two stages: (1) the corpus-wide lexeme document-frequency ceiling runs first and admits outright if the rarest lexeme is discriminating enough; (2) ONLY IF that refuses, and ONLY IF the request carries a narrowing filter (court, courts, dateFrom, dateTo or caseType), the server COUNTS the eligible population with the same predicates the ranker will apply, stopping early at a cap, and admits when the population is at or under it. A capped probe proves only 'at least the cap' and never admits - unknown is not small. An admitted query is then ranked inside a MATERIALIZED fence so the structured predicates run before the text index.

notEnumeratedHere.rule: This registry enumerates the capabilities v1 SHIPS or has adjudicated. Its schema does not require exhaustive enumeration of every capability the product does not have, and adding rows for absent features would invent a feature taxonomy in a Gate-B convergence round.
notEnumeratedHere.drafting: Document drafting has NO row. It is absent by prohibition, not by oversight: no generation capability is ENABLED, generation.evidence_from_passages is POST_V1 on every platform, and no drafting claim is permitted by the claims register.
notEnumeratedHere.hearingPack: Hearing Pack has NO row, for the same reason, and briefing.daily_loop - the nearest shipped-adjacent thing - is DISABLED_NOT_READY on every platform.
notEnumeratedHere.classification: NON_GATE_P1_BACKLOG. Neither absence blocks Gate B and neither authorises a claim. If a future round decides the registry must enumerate absent capabilities, that is a schema decision and gets its own CCR.
